items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I remember the Jack Teagarden was playing in the band... That band -- that was one of the hottest bands, one of the greatest bands that I ever heard.

ctx.x: 1930 was a rough year. Yes, it was rough that year, so we regrouped, we finished that summer and regrouped back in Cincinnati, and we got the old band back together again. That's when Alphonso Trent hired Cy Oliver to write for the band. So we was offered a job in Cleveland, at the Hollywood Club, a nightclub, They knew about Trent's band, so we opened on a New Year's eve night.

They had two bands. I remember the Jack Teagarden was playing in the band, another Teagarden was playing trumpet Ray Bauduc was playing drums, and I can't think who was playing the reed section. The name of the band skips me right now, it'll come to be in a few minutes. That band -- that was one of the hottest bands, one of the greatest bands that I ever heard. And that band opened up New Year's eve night and we had to go on behind that band and we never -- I never sweated so hard in all my life. That was a great…

That evening the band left and was paid off. The next night was New Year's night, the crowd was small. And just seemed like the crowds never did pick up. So after working there about -- about three and a half or four weeks, the club closed. So there we were, so we decided to leave Cleveland, and go West.
